info.name: TravelVIP - Wallet Activity
info.description:
GET /v1/wallet/activity and GET /v1/wallet/activity/{id} - the authenticated partner's own wallet ledger, curated (contract in wallet-activity-api.md).

Runs against your existing **TravelVIP Local Env** - it needs only two keys you already have:
- `base_url`
- `access_token` - decides which wallet is read; there is no partner id anywhere in the path, query or body

No `external_api_key`, no `signing_key`, no `Idempotency-Key`. Those five gates guard the top-up because it moves money; these endpoints only read the caller's own rows, so the access token is the only credential. If you are used to the top-up request, that difference is deliberate, not an omission.

The collection WRITES (every send):
- `request_id`, `correlation_id` - generated per request, echoed back on errors
- `activity_id` - captured by 'Activity feed' from the newest entry, so 'Activity detail' can be sent straight afterwards with no copy-paste

Run the folder top to bottom: the two happy paths first (the feed hands the detail request its id), then the four contract checks, which are expected to fail with 400/401/404 and pass their tests by doing so.

Amounts here are **decimal rupees**, unlike the top-up collection, which is in paise. Same wallet, two different contracts - the read surface sits next to /v1/partners/me, which has always been in major units.

request.description:
Newest first, 15 per page. An outstanding hold appears as `funds_held` / `kind: hold` while its funds are still reserved, then drops out once it settles and is replaced by whatever settled it - so the same money is never counted twice. `summary` is the balance NOW, not as of this page, so it does not change as you page through.

Money fields are decimal rupees. A null amount means the wallet did not report that field - treat it as unknown, never as zero.

One reference field, `reference` - Paynex's `referenceId` and `bookingId` are merged into it (booking reference last), so a hold-derived movement still reports its booking.

request.description:
A five-value union on `type`.

- `hold` / `committed` / `released` / `expired` - one shape in four settlement states: the held / committed / released figures plus `legs`, one entry per step. There is no `status` field; `type` is the state.
- `transaction` - a standalone movement: no `legs`, nothing to break down

`{id}` takes a feed entry id or a hold id - the wallet resolves either, so a hold you created stays reachable after it drops out of the feed.

`activity_id` is set for you by request 1.

request.description: A bad page is rejected here rather than passed to the wallet, which would answer with an empty feed - and an empty feed reads as 'you have no activity'.
